_note: Invented articles for the demo edition. Places, people, outlets and events are fictional.

articles.title: Westmark legislature passes water rights bill
articles.summary: The Westmark legislature voted 61-48 on Tuesday to pass a bill that caps agricultural water withdrawals from the Selby River basin during droughts. The bill now goes to Governor Dana Ruiz, who has said she will sign it.

articles.title: Water rights bill heads to Westmark governor after 61-48 vote
articles.summary: Westmark lawmakers approved limits on drought-time water withdrawals from the Selby River basin. Farm groups opposed the bill; cities in the basin supported it.

articles.title: Landmark water bill wins passage, a historic victory for Selby River towns
articles.summary: In a historic vote, the Westmark legislature passed a water rights bill that caps drought withdrawals from the Selby River basin, a win for towns that saw wells run dry last summer.

articles.title: Westmark passes Selby River water cap over farm lobby objections
articles.summary: The legislature voted 61-48 for the Selby River basin withdrawal cap. Governor Ruiz is expected to sign the water rights bill this week.

articles.title: Lawmakers ram through costly water grab that farmers say will slash harvests
articles.summary: Westmark legislators rammed through a water rights bill capping Selby River basin withdrawals. The state farm bureau says the cap could cut irrigated acreage by a fifth in drought years.

articles.title: Selby River farmers brace for water limits after legislature vote
articles.summary: Farmers in the Selby River basin say the water rights bill passed 61-48 by the Westmark legislature will force them to fallow fields during droughts.

articles.title: Westmark water bill passes; farm bureau vows court challenge
articles.summary: The Westmark farm bureau said it will challenge the Selby River water rights bill in court once the governor signs it.

articles.title: Valdoria central bank holds benchmark rate at 4.25%
articles.summary: The Central Bank of Valdoria left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 4.25% for a third straight meeting, citing inflation of 3.1% that remains above its 2% target.

articles.title: Valdoria keeps interest rates on hold as inflation lingers
articles.summary: Valdoria's central bank kept its benchmark rate at 4.25% and said it expects inflation to ease toward its 2% target next year.

articles.title: Valdoria central bank stands pat on rates, pointing to stubborn inflation
articles.summary: The Central Bank of Valdoria held its benchmark interest rate at 4.25%, with officials pointing to 3.1% inflation.

articles.title: Valdoria holds interest rate steady for third meeting
articles.summary: Valdoria's central bank left its benchmark rate at 4.25%. Two of seven board members voted for a cut, according to the bank's statement.

articles.title: Storm floods Port Avery waterfront, cutting power to 18,000
articles.summary: A coastal storm pushed seawater into downtown Port Avery on Tuesday night, cutting power to about 18,000 customers. No deaths were reported.

articles.title: Port Avery flooding: power out for 18,000 as storm surge hits downtown
articles.summary: Storm surge flooded the Port Avery waterfront and downtown. The utility said power could take two days to restore for some customers.

articles.title: Port Avery storm leaves downtown flooded and thousands without power
articles.summary: About 18,000 Port Avery customers lost power after a storm surge flooded the waterfront. The mayor declared a local emergency.

articles.title: Port Avery declares emergency after storm surge floods downtown
articles.summary: Port Avery's mayor declared a local emergency after a storm surge flooded downtown and cut power to about 18,000 customers. No deaths were reported.

articles.title: Ethics board opens probe into Governor Ruiz's travel spending
articles.summary: The Westmark ethics board confirmed it is reviewing Governor Dana Ruiz's use of state aircraft for trips that included political events. Her office called the trips official business.

articles.title: Ruiz faces ethics review over state aircraft trips
articles.summary: Westmark's ethics board is reviewing Governor Ruiz's travel on state aircraft. The governor's office said all trips were official business.

articles.title: Westmark ethics board reviewing governor's travel on state aircraft
articles.summary: The state ethics board said it opened a review of Governor Dana Ruiz's state aircraft travel after a complaint was filed in October.

articles.title: Westmark University students rally against 9% tuition increase
articles.summary: Several hundred Westmark University students rallied outside the regents' meeting to oppose a proposed 9% tuition increase for next fall.

articles.title: Students protest proposed Westmark University tuition hike
articles.summary: Students rallied against a proposed 9% tuition increase at Westmark University. Regents will vote on the tuition plan in December.

articles.title: Westmark University regents delay tuition vote after student rally
articles.summary: Westmark University regents postponed a vote on a 9% tuition increase to December after hundreds of students rallied outside their meeting.

articles.title: Brightline recalls 42,000 e-bikes over battery fire risk
articles.summary: E-bike maker Brightline is recalling about 42,000 bikes after reports of batteries overheating while charging. Owners can get a free replacement battery.

articles.title: Brightline e-bike recall: 42,000 bikes affected by battery overheating
articles.summary: Brightline said it received 31 reports of e-bike batteries overheating while charging, including four small fires, and is recalling about 42,000 bikes.

articles.title: Brightline pulls 42,000 e-bikes after battery fires
articles.summary: Brightline is recalling about 42,000 e-bikes after reports of battery fires during charging and is offering free replacement batteries.

articles.title: Drought-tolerant wheat strain matches yields in three-year field trial
articles.summary: Researchers at the Halvorsen Agricultural Institute reported that a drought-tolerant wheat strain matched standard yields in a three-year field trial, and outyielded them by 12% in the driest year.

articles.title: New wheat strain holds up in drought, Halvorsen field trial finds
articles.summary: A drought-tolerant wheat strain developed at the Halvorsen Agricultural Institute produced yields similar to standard wheat over three years of field trials.

articles.title: Final rule: reporting requirements for rural broadband grant recipients
articles.summary: The Westmark Department of Commerce finalized a rule requiring rural broadband grant recipients to report connection speeds and household sign-ups every six months. The rule takes effect January 15.

articles.title: Opinion: State of Westmark v. Harlan Mining Co.
articles.summary: The Westmark Supreme Court ruled 5-2 that the state may require Harlan Mining Co. to fund cleanup of tailings ponds at mines closed before 1990. The court sent the case back to a lower court to set the amount.

articles.title: H.B. 412: Rural Hospital Staffing Act
articles.summary: Latest action on 2026-11-03: Passed House by recorded vote, 70-39.

articles.title: Contract award: armory repair program
articles.summary: The Westmark Department of Defense awarded a $48 million contract to Caldera Construction to repair 12 National Guard armories. Work is expected to be completed in 2028.

articles.title: Harbor City stadium gets new name in sponsorship deal
articles.summary: Harbor City's football stadium will be renamed under a 10-year sponsorship deal announced Tuesday.

articles.title: Celebrity chef opens third restaurant in Lakeside
articles.summary: A celebrity chef opened a third restaurant in the Lakeside neighborhood this week.
